children: REC and Larsen & Toubro raise Rs 500 crore each as DLT-based securities are tested within India’s regulated market infrastructure

The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has enabled tokenised corporate bond issuances worth a combined Rs 1,000 crore by REC and Larsen & Toubro on its Electronic Bidding Platform (NSE EBP). The transactions were conducted under the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s (SEBI) Regulatory Sandbox Framework.

REC raised Rs 500 crore through the first tokenised corporate bond issuance on NSE EBP on September 7, followed by a Rs 500 crore issuance by Larsen & Toubro on September 9. The transactions mark an early application of tokenisation in India’s regulated corporate bond market, NSE said in a release.

REC’s issuance had a base size of Rs 100 crore and a green shoe option of Rs 400 crore. It received overall subscription of 7.9 times the base issue, with REC accepting Rs 500 crore at a coupon rate of 7.30 per cent.

The issuance saw participation from banks, financial institutions, mutual funds and depositories. The subsequent Larsen & Toubro issuance demonstrated the application of the technology by a private-sector issuer, NSE said.

Tokenisation enables securities to be represented and managed digitally using Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT). The technology allows digital records of securities to be maintained across a distributed network, with NSE positioning it as a tool for improving processes across the securities lifecycle.

NSE said the technology is designed to facilitate atomic settlement, improve transparency and enhance operational efficiency across the securities lifecycle. The system also uses India’s existing digital settlement infrastructure, rather than requiring a separate settlement framework.

The initiative was enabled under the Sebi Regulatory Sandbox Framework, with guidance and support from SEBI and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The framework provided the regulatory setting for testing the tokenisation technology within India’s existing capital-market infrastructure.

The technology was formally unveiled on September 10 at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey. NSE said the two issuances mark a step towards broader adoption of tokenisation in the corporate bond market.

NSE is committed to be at the forefront of technology-led innovation in India’s capital markets, said Viral Mody, Executive Director - Vertical 1 (Critical Operations), NSE. Mody said the successful implementation of tokenisation for corporate bonds demonstrated NSE’s ability to translate emerging technologies into “scalable solutions for regulated market infrastructure”.

He further added that NSE remains committed to advancing technology-led market infrastructure that is “trusted, resilient, transparent and responsive” to the evolving needs of issuers, investors and other market participants. The two issuances provide an initial demonstration of how tokenisation can be integrated into regulated corporate bond transactions.
